scope.question: Does stopping admission of new equal-depth catch-up tournaments after a fixed share of the hard budget improve the promoted selective-backtracking policy?
scope.policy: An already-admitted tournament finishes. Once completed catch-up probe work reaches 20%, 25%, or 30% of the fixed hard budget, later signal crossings are suppressed.
scope.selection_surface: Exact canonical seed identities in disjoint 16-seed blocks; the two active believer_impact_56s specifications plus unchanged controls.
scope.non_claim: This rejects a blind cumulative work quota at 750k. It does not reject budget-aware selective backtracking or policies that estimate the value of each tournament.

offline_lead.observation: At a 30% quota, the first 16-seed panel would have suppressed ten later tournaments, all of which eventually retained the current prefix.
offline_lead.interpretation: This justified a live causal test but was not itself performance evidence.

decision.action: Do not promote any quota arm and do not spend a canonical V2 run on quota-30.
decision.reason: The apparent first-block gain decayed monotonically on fresh seed blocks, the combined effect is negligible relative to its uncertainty, and the source effects have opposite signs.
decision.design_lesson: Late tournaments are not uniformly wasteful. A successor must distinguish estimated tournament value or improve the equal-depth selection decision instead of stopping solely because cumulative probe work crossed a percentage.
